Peggy Flanagan is an American politician, educator, advocate, and Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party leader. She currently serves as Minnesota’s 50th lieutenant  governor. Flanagan became lieutenant governor in 2019 after winning election alongside  Governor Tim Walz.

Born Peggy Flanagan on September 22, 1979, she grew up in St. Louis Park, Minnesota. She belongs to the White Earth Band of Ojibwe and has become a prominent Native American  political leader. Moreover, she graduated from St. Louis Park Public Schools before attending the University of Minnesota. She earned a bachelor’s degree in American Indian studies and child psychology in 2002.

Flanagan began her public service career on the Minneapolis Board of Education, where she served from 2005 to 2009. She later worked at Wellstone Action and trained organizers, candidates, and elected officials. Additionally, she became executive director of the Children’s Defense Fund-Minnesota. In 2015, voters elected her to the Minnesota House of Representatives, where she represented communities including St. Louis Park.

As lieutenant governor, Flanagan has focused on children, working families, housing, childcare, and Indigenous communities. She also helped advance the state’s Missing and Murdered Indigenous Relatives Office and affordable housing investments.

In 2026, Flanagan is running for the U.S. Senate seat being vacated by Tina Smith. She secured the DFL endorsement in May, while U.S. Representative Angie Craig continues challenging her in the August 11 primary. If Flanagan wins, she could become the first Native American woman elected to the U.S. Senate.

Peggy Flanagan Age | How Old is Peggy Flanagan?

Peggy Flanagan is 46 years old as of August 2026. She was born on September 22, 1979, in St. Louis Park, Minnesota. Flanagan will turn 47 on September 22, 2026. Moreover, she currently serves as Minnesota’s lieutenant governor and is running for the U.S. Senate in the 2026 election. She entered statewide politics in 2018 as Tim Walz’s running mate. Additionally, Flanagan became Minnesota’s first Native American woman elected to statewide office. Her political career now spans more than two decades, including service on the Minneapolis school board and Minnesota House of Representatives.

Peggy Flanagan Political Party | Is She a Democrat or Republican?

Peggy Flanagan is a Democrat and a member of Minnesota’s Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party (DFL). The DFL serves as Minnesota’s affiliate of the national Democratic Party. Moreover, Flanagan has held Democratic office throughout her political career, including service in the Minnesota House and as lieutenant governor. She currently serves as Minnesota’s lieutenant governor and is running for the U.S. Senate in 2026. Additionally, the DFL endorsed Flanagan for the Senate race. Her campaign focuses on supporting working families, protecting healthcare, expanding education opportunities, and defending reproductive rights. Flanagan has also emphasized housing affordability and support for Indigenous communities.

Peggy Flanagan Education

Peggy Flanagan graduated from St. Louis Park Public Schools in Minnesota. She later attended the University of Minnesota, where she completed her undergraduate studies. In 2002, Flanagan earned a bachelor’s degree in American Indian Studies and child psychology. Her academic background combined Indigenous studies with an understanding of children and families. Moreover, this education complemented her later advocacy work involving children, education, and Indigenous communities. After college, she pursued nonprofit leadership and public service. Her University of Minnesota education became an important foundation for her political career and advocacy work. Flanagan later served on the Minneapolis Board of Education and Minnesota House of Representatives.

Peggy Flanagan Ethnicity

Peggy Flanagan is Ojibwe and an enrolled member of the White Earth Nation in Minnesota. She comes from an Indigenous and Irish family background, according to her current campaign biography. Moreover, Flanagan proudly identifies as an Ojibwe woman and has spoken openly about her Native heritage. She grew up in St. Louis Park, Minnesota, while maintaining strong connections to her tribal community. Additionally, her Ojibwe identity has shaped her public service and advocacy for Indigenous communities. Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to statewide executive office in Minnesota. She now serves as Minnesota’s lieutenant  governor and is running for the U.S. Senate in 2026.

Peggy Flanagan Husband | Is Peggy Flanagan married?

Peggy Flanagan is married to Tom Weber, a former Minnesota Public Radio reporter and radio host. The couple married on September 14, 2019, in Red Wing, Minnesota. Weber previously worked for Minnesota Public Radio before leaving the station in 2018. Moreover, he and Flanagan announced their engagement several months before their wedding. Flanagan has a daughter, Siobhan, from a previous marriage. Today, Peggy and Tom live in St. Louis Park, Minnesota, with Siobhan and their dog, Reuben. Additionally, Flanagan continues serving as Minnesota’s lieutenant governor while campaigning for the U.S. Senate in 2026. Tom Weber remains a supportive partner as Flanagan balances her  political career and family life.

Peggy Flanagan First Husband

Peggy Flanagan’s first husband was Tim Hellendrung. The couple had a daughter, Siobhan, during their marriage. However, their marriage ended in 2017. Flanagan later began a relationship with former Minnesota Public Radio host Tom Weber in 2018. The couple married in September 2019 and continue raising their family in St. Louis Park, Minnesota. Moreover, Flanagan and Weber live with Siobhan and their pets. Unlike her public political career, Flanagan keeps details about her first marriage relatively private. Today, she serves as Minnesota’s lieutenant governor and is running for the U.S. Senate in the 2026 election.

Peggy Flanagan Children | Daughter

Peggy Flanagan has one daughter, Siobhan, from her previous marriage to Tim Hellendrung. Siobhan was born before Flanagan entered statewide  politics and remains her only publicly identified child. Moreover, Siobhan is 13 years old as of 2026 and has developed an interest in theater. Flanagan has spoken about balancing motherhood with her political career and current Senate campaign. Additionally, Siobhan sometimes volunteers at her mother’s campaign office on weekends. Flanagan and her husband, Tom Weber, live with Siobhan in St. Louis Park, Minnesota. Her experience as a mother continues shaping her advocacy for children, families, education, and affordable childcare.

Peggy Flanagan Family | Parents and Siblings

Peggy Flanagan was raised by her mother, Pat Flanagan, and father, Marvin Manypenny. Her mother moved the family to St. Louis Park, Minnesota, during Flanagan’s childhood. Meanwhile, her father maintained ties to the White Earth Reservation. Both parents strongly influenced Flanagan’s values, identity, and public service career. Sadly, both parents died during her first term as lieutenant governor. Flanagan has spoken about their lasting influence on her life and political work. Moreover, she identifies as a citizen of the White Earth Nation of Ojibwe. Public Minnesota legislative records do not identify any biological siblings. Therefore, information about Peggy Flanagan’s brothers and sisters remains limited.

Politics

Peggy Flanagan for U.S. Senate | Campaign, Primary, Polls, Endorsements & Election

Peggy Flanagan is running for the U.S. Senate in Minnesota’s 2026 election. She entered the race in February 2025 to replace retiring Senator Tina Smith. Flanagan currently serves as Minnesota’s lieutenant governor and secured the DFL Party endorsement in May 2026. However, U.S. Representative Angie Craig declined to seek the endorsement and advanced directly to the August 11 Democratic primary. The primary includes Flanagan, Craig, and other candidates.

Geographic Reference

The Democratic primary has become a major contest between Flanagan’s progressive campaign and Craig’s more moderate approach. Recent polling gives Flanagan a clear advantage in the primary. A May Democratic survey showed Flanagan leading Craig 55% to 25% among respondents. Another recent poll reported Flanagan ahead 46% to 32%. Flanagan has received support from progressive leaders, including Senator Bernie Sanders, while Craig emphasizes her congressional experience and general-election strength.

The Minnesota Democratic primary takes place on August 11, 2026, with the general election scheduled for November 3. Flanagan campaigns on healthcare, reproductive rights, working-family policies, and limiting corporate influence. She also opposes corporate PAC and AIPAC contributions. Meanwhile, the Republican field includes candidates competing for the chance to challenge the Democratic nominee. If Flanagan wins the Senate election, she could become the first Native American woman elected to the U.S. Senate.

Peggy Flanagan Policies and Political Views

Peggy Flanagan is a progressive Democrat who supports Medicare for All and universal healthcare. She also backs protecting abortion access and reproductive healthcare nationwide. Moreover, Flanagan supports universal childcare and paid family and medical leave. She has emphasized affordable housing and policies that help working families.

Legislative Branch

On immigration, Flanagan supports major changes to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). She has criticized mass deportations and opposed policies expanding federal immigration enforcement. Additionally, she supports stronger protections for immigrant communities. Flanagan also advocates for Indigenous rights, tribal consultation, gun safety reforms, and transgender rights. Her 2026 Senate campaign positions her firmly within the Democratic Party’s progressive wing.

Peggy Flanagan vs Angie Craig | Senate Primary, Polls, Policies & Key Differences

Peggy Flanagan and Angie Craig are competing for Minnesota’s Democratic U.S. Senate nomination on August 11, 2026. The winner will challenge the Republican nominee in November. Flanagan serves as Minnesota’s lieutenant  governor, while Craig represents Minnesota’s 2nd Congressional District. Flanagan secured the Minnesota DFL endorsement on May 30, after Craig chose to bypass the party endorsement process. Craig instead went directly to the statewide primary.

The race highlights a clear ideological difference within Minnesota Democrats. Flanagan represents the party’s progressive wing, supporting Medicare for All, stronger reproductive rights, and limits on corporate  political influence. Craig presents herself as a pragmatic Democrat with experience winning competitive congressional races. Immigration has also become a major issue. Craig faced criticism for supporting the Laken Riley Act before later expressing regret over her vote. Flanagan has strongly criticized expanded ICE enforcement.

Flanagan currently holds an advantage in several Democratic primary polls. A July poll showed her leading Craig 46% to 32% among likely Democratic primary voters. However, Craig has raised substantially more campaign money and argues that her electoral record gives Democrats broader statewide appeal. Both candidates have intensified their campaigns ahead of Tuesday’s primary. The August 11 result will determine whether Minnesota chooses Flanagan’s progressive approach or Craig’s more moderate strategy for the November Senate election.

Journalism & News Industry

Peggy Flanagan AIPAC | Israel, Gaza, Campaign Donations & 2026 Senate Race

Peggy Flanagan has rejected AIPAC campaign money during her 2026 U.S. Senate campaign. She says her values do not align with AIPAC’s current political agenda. Moreover, Flanagan has criticized AIPAC’s influence in Democratic primary elections and national  politics. During a June debate, she contrasted her position with opponent Angie Craig’s support from AIPAC-linked spending. Flanagan has made opposition to corporate PAC money a central part of her campaign.

The AIPAC issue has become a major dividing point between Flanagan and Craig. Flanagan supports limiting U.S. military assistance to Israel and has criticized Israel’s conduct in Gaza. Meanwhile, Craig has accepted support from AIPAC and defended her relationship with pro-Israel political groups. The dispute reflects broader divisions among Democrats over Israel, Gaza, and U.S. foreign policy.

Flanagan’s campaign says she does not accept corporate PAC contributions, emphasizing grassroots fundraising instead. The Federal Election Commission reports millions in contributions to her campaign, largely from individual donors. Therefore, AIPAC remains an important issue in Minnesota’s Democratic Senate primary. Flanagan’s position has helped distinguish her progressive campaign from Craig’s more moderate approach.

Peggy Flanagan Salary

Peggy Flanagan earns $105,038 annually as Minnesota’s lieutenant governor in fiscal year 2026. The Minnesota Compensation Council set this salary for the state’s constitutional officers. Moreover, the figure increased from $101,123 in fiscal year 2025. Flanagan has served as lieutenant governor since January 2019 alongside Governor Tim Walz. Additionally, her salary comes from her official state position and does not include campaign funds. She is currently campaigning for the U.S. Senate in Minnesota’s 2026 election. Her lieutenant governor salary remains the official compensation figure for fiscal year 2026.

Therefore, claims assigning her a specific net worth should be treated cautiously. Flanagan earns a salary as Minnesota’s lieutenant governor and has held several public and nonprofit leadership positions. Moreover, her 2026 Senate campaign has raised millions, but those funds belong to her campaign. Campaign contributions do not represent Peggy Flanagan’s personal net worth.
